research_repo.note: metric CSVs are untracked run outputs; the commit identifies the scripts

paper_figure.label: fig:heatmap
paper_figure.reproduces: grids.synthetic.post_hoc + grids.synthetic.in_generation, conditions in this order

metric: TPR@1%FPR (%), column tpr_far01 of T4_full_grid.csv times 100, for both families (post-hoc methods in identity mode)

category_names.C4: Model-based attack followed by multiple perturbations

grid_notes.synthetic: Paper figure. Post-hoc = the 1,593-image synthetic subset (identity payload); in-generation = the 1,193-image matched cohort.
grid_notes.manipulated: Not a paper figure: the same 52 conditions on the 1,600 manipulated images (T4_full_grid.csv category label for manipulated images), post-hoc only.
grid_notes.real: Not a paper figure: the same 52 conditions on the 1,600 real images, post-hoc only. UnMarker and unmarkshare are null for the 7 sentence-capable methods: on real images their UnMarker conditions were run on the sentence-payload images only, so the identity-mode grid has no value (tab_unmarker prints '--').
grid_notes.post_hoc_n: Number of attacked watermarked images behind each cell (T4 column n).
grid_notes.post_hoc_attribution_acc: Open-set attribution accuracy at 1% FPR (%) over the 100-identity codebook, T4 column acc. Not shown in the paper figure.

mean_asi.note: T4_full_grid.csv has no ASI column. These values are computed by build_data.py from robust_curves.csv (column x = condition-level mean ASI) as the mean over methods; synthetic_post_hoc pools the two synthetic identity arms per method weighted by n_pos. They are not printed in the paper. The paper's own mean-ASI values (matched cohort) are in attacks.json.
